children: Aetna unit on Thursday announced a companywide initiative to offer a single prior authorization across all cancer types as the health insurer seeks to remove a key administrative burden for medical practitioners.

The initiative comes amid an industrywide push to cut back on prior authorizations, a process healthcare providers should follow to obtain coverage approvals from health plans before conducting certain non-emergency medical procedures.

The company said that beginning Sept. 1, prior authorization bundles covering a range of cancer treatments, including chemotherapy as well as radiation oncology services where appropriate, will be available to Aetna members in eligible Medicaid states.
Full rollout of the initiative is expected to get underway across all Aetna business lines next year.
The move builds on the success of the initial rollout, as part of which Aetna offered a bundled prior authorization for nearly 25% of eligible members.
